text:
Ellen: Quick — Redwood POC for Meridian Health needs Private deployment network handoff. They want peering + on-prem NAT. Need a one-pager I can send their cloud team.

Jon: Key asks: full list of customer CIDRs, preferred connection (peering vs PrivateLink), RTB IDs to update, AZ/subnet targets, and any egress IPs we should expect from their NAT.

Ellen: Customer provided: 10.60.0.0/16 (apps), 10.61.0.0/20 (datacenter). They prefer peering.

Priya: For peering we require: 1) Confirm non-overlap with Redwood control plane CIDR (10.200.0.0/16). 2) Add a route in their RTB: dest=10.200.0.0/16 -> pcx-XXXXX. 3) We add route: dest=10.60.0.0/16 -> pcx-XXXXX. 4) Enable DNS resolution on the peering options.

Jon: Example CLI for them to paste:```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0aa11bb22 --destination-cidr-block 10.200.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0f1e2d3c
aws ec2 modify-vpc-peering-connection-options --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0f1e2d3c --accepter-peering-connection-options \"{\"AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc\":true}\" --requester-peering-connection-options \"{\"AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc\":true}\"
```They must replace IDs.

Priya: Networking caveat: do not propagate customer IGW/0.0.0.0/0 into the peered RTBs. If they have a centralized NAT, we need the NAT EIP(s) so our egress ACLs can allow outbound model calls.

Ellen: They asked about Private DNS for internal hostnames. What's the quickest setup?

Priya: For DNS we can do two options: 1) VPC peering + Route53 resolver rules (inbound/outbound) where they forward queries for our zones to our resolver; OR 2) PrivateLink with interface endpoints which gives per-AZ ENIs and standard AWS interface endpoint DNS. For short POC, peering + resolver rule is usually faster if they can update RT and security groups.

Jon: Security note: Management plane needs TCP/443 (our side) from their peered subnets. We prefer to provide the ENI addresses for least privilege. For POC we can accept the peered CIDR but add a ticket to tighten to ENIs before prod. Also include TLS fingerprint if they need it for the security questionnaire.

Ellen: They also asked about cross-account IAM roles so their engineers can accept the peering automatically via CI. Any extra steps?

Priya: They can create an assume-role with a resource policy allowing us to accept the peering, or just accept manually. If using automation we need the role ARN and a short-lived token scope (we sign an aud claim). We'll add that as optional.

Jon: If they insist on PrivateLink instead: we'll provide a service name (com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-...) and they must create interface endpoints in each AZ and grant SG rules to allow HTTPS to our endpoint SG. PrivateLink avoids route changes but requires per-AZ endpoints and DNS validation. Slightly longer to stand up.

Ellen: Any sample security questionnaire wording I can paste?

Priya: Use: "Redwood requires VPC peering or PrivateLink for private POC deployments. Routes must explicitly point at Redwood control plane CIDR (10.200.0.0/16). TLS 1.2+ enforced; mutual TLS recommended for production. Management plane access limited to peered CIDRs or specified ENI IPs. No default route (0.0.0.0/0) propagation into peered tables."

Jon: Also add: "For DNS, either Route53 resolver inbound rules or interface endpoints are supported; customers must provision resolver rules or endpoint per AZ."

infra-bot: Note: staging deploys will be blocked until peering is accepted. Create support ticket S-12345 to track NAT EIP and RTB IDs.

Ellen: Great — I'll send this and request RTB IDs, NAT EIPs, and whether they want automation via assume-role. Will update when they reply. :thumbsup:
